script.analysis: All 19,032 stored characters read in two contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Second-person hook (first salary, lifestyle upgrade, stuck after 3 years); composite Tyler (27, $62K) losing "$800K-$1.5M by 40". Ten mistakes each with a statistic and opportunity-cost figure: (1) salary negotiation (Babcock lifetime gap, hiring-manager survey), (2) delaying investing ($300/month from 22 vs 32), median Gen Z balance, Fidelity 1x by 30, unclaimed match, (3) $38K SUV at $650 for 72 months and average $795 payment, (4) $5,200 at 22% on declining minimums, (5) lifestyle creep and half-the-raise rule, (6) $400 rent upgrade, renter cost burden, (7) gross vs net pay ($5,166 vs $3,380), (8) peer spending and social-media FOMO stats, (9) 631 credit score and refinance gap, (10) forgotten subscriptions; cumulative tally $3.7M-$4.1M and system-incentives close. Dense, concrete and well-paced, with mixed accuracy and non-additive totals. No sponsor CTA. ASR fragment ("He invested the raise exactly what he invested exactly") preserved; not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:9500 Negotiation: Linda Babcock's research is often summarized as a lifetime gap of roughly $500K-$1M+ from not negotiating a first salary - "$600,000-$1.5 million" is a loose paraphrase; the script later calls the loss "conservatively $400,000" and earlier "over a million", internally inconsistent. Hiring-manager survey ("over 50,000", 76% room, 64% accept, 94% kept) unsourced. $300/month from 22 vs 32 to 62: at 10% ~$1.90M vs ~$678K (script $1.9M / $680K, correct at 10%; at 7% ~$787K vs ~$366K). Unclaimed $1,500/year match over 40 years ~$299K (7%) to ~$664K (10%), matches the stated range. Median Gen Z balance $4,800 unverified.

0:9500 Car: $650/month for 6 years invested then left to age 60 grows to ~$412K at 7% or ~$1.01M at 10%; the script gives $660,000 and two sentences later calls it "a $513,000 decision" - inconsistent. $5,200 at 22% with 1%-plus-interest minimums repays in ~234 months (~19.5 years) totaling ~$13,700, matching "closer to $14,000" but not "over 30 years" (duration depends on minimum formula).

9500:19032 $400/month for 30 years at 10% = ~$904K, matches $904,000 (7% gives ~$488K); $150/month for 30 years at 10% = ~$339K, matches. $62,000/12 = $5,166 and gap to $3,380 = $1,786 correct. 22.6 million cost-burdened renter households consistent with Harvard JCHS. 680 vs 760 on a $300K mortgage costing $50K-$80K lifetime plausible depending on rate spread. Subscription underestimate ~$133 consistent with C+R-type surveys; Empower 51% and Gen Z FOMO 70% unverified.

9500:19032 The $3.7M-$4.1M "total" sums opportunity costs computed at different horizons and returns that overlap (e.g., delayed investing, raises and rent compete for the same dollars) and mixes lost earnings with lost investment growth; it is not additive for one person on a $62K salary. "Every dollar in your 20s becomes $10-15" consistent with 7% over ~35-40 years.
